nodes.label: Action Manifest Pattern (Single Source of Truth for Actions)
nodes.rationale: Introduced to eliminate cross-runtime string parity fragility between Python and Unity. Before this, action names, parameters, required_capabilities, and engine command types lived in three separate locations with no enforced consistency — a typo between Python and Unity produced a silent failure. YAML chosen for human readability; JSON sidecar generated for Unity because Unity has no built-in YAML parser for arbitrary files. Handler class paths intentionally excluded from the manifest to avoid coupling it to Python class paths.
nodes.norm_label: action manifest pattern (single source of truth for actions)

nodes.label: Role System (Named Capability+Brain Bundles)
nodes.rationale: Roles are flat, not hierarchical, to avoid traversal algorithms, merge-order ambiguity, and circular-extends failure modes. Capabilities from agent and role are unioned (not one-wins) so per-agent specialisation beyond the role remains possible. Role name stored in agent.metadata rather than a new Agent field to avoid additive API surface — metadata already flows through snapshots, events, and brain context.

nodes.label: Capability Gate / Tag System
nodes.rationale: Capabilities are OR-intersection filters (agent sees action if capabilities overlap), not AND (would require agents to hold every tag). Not a security enforcement mechanism — they filter what the brain is shown, not what can be physically executed. A brain that constructs an Intent for a gated action will fail at validate_intent() because the action won't be in the agent's visible schema set.

nodes.label: AgentOwnershipMode (BindToExisting vs CreateAtRuntime)
nodes.rationale: BindToExisting: agent declared in YAML, Unity attaches visual shell only, no RPC sent. CreateAtRuntime: Unity owns lifecycle, sends register/unregister RPCs. Phase 4 audit flags 'ownership' as a misleading name — the actual difference is who drives agent lifecycle, not who owns data (Python always owns all agent state). Proposed rename to AgentLifecycleMode.

nodes.label: AgentView Immutability Pattern
nodes.rationale: AgentRuntime never passes a mutable Agent to brains, handlers, or worlds. It wraps in AgentView — a frozen snapshot valid only for one step. Handlers that want to change inventory must return ActionResult with state_mutations; the runtime applies mutations after the handler returns. This makes mutation auditable and snapshotable, and prevents order-of-execution bugs in the simultaneous scheduler.

nodes.label: ActionKind Enum (Advisory LLM Label)
nodes.rationale: ActionKind (HOST/ENGINE/HYBRID) has zero runtime dispatch effect. Its only effect is appending a label to the action description in the LLM system prompt. Phase 4 audit flags this as a misleading name that implies behavioral constraints that are unenforced. Proposed rename to ActionHint or ActionExecution with explicit 'advisory only' documentation.

nodes.label: Snapshot/Restore Protocol (pickle-based)
nodes.rationale: Uses Python pickle with per-process HMAC-SHA256 signing. Known design debt: not cross-process portable, not version-stable, not inspectable. The serialize()/restore() protocol on each component already provides the right interface — the outer SimulationSnapshot container just needs to switch to a JSON/msgpack format with explicit version fields.

nodes.label: Tick Execution Sequence (Hot Path)
nodes.rationale: Per-tick: ObservationRegistry providers (lowest priority) merged with world.observe() then engine-injected fields (highest priority, always overwrite). SimultaneousScheduler dispatches all brain.decide() calls concurrently via asyncio.gather; action results applied in completion order — a known intra-tick snapshot vs. application ordering tradeoff accepted for throughput.

nodes.label: HostedWorld / ExternalWorld Pattern
nodes.rationale: World whose authoritative state is provided by an external host (Unity). Engine runs cognition; host pushes observations and receives engine_commands. Phase 4 audit notes the name 'HostedWorld' is ambiguous ('hosted' could mean hosted by the server). Protocol it implements is already named ExternalWorld; renaming the class would align the two names.

nodes.label: EventBus (Synchronous Pub/Sub)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous, not async, by design: simple, predictable, debuggable. All cross-cutting effects (social graph, logging, event streaming) go through events rather than direct coupling — this is an architectural invariant. SocialEffectSubscriber is the only mechanism to update the social graph; handlers must emit side_effects, the engine does not infer social effects.

nodes.label: WebSocket Protocol v1
nodes.rationale: JSON over WebSocket, text frames, no binary encoding. Frame types: hlo (hello), req (request), res (response), evt (event). Known debt: dual agent registration wire formats (register_agent flat params vs agent.register dot-notation) — a versioning artifact adding handler dispatch complexity. Phase 4 recommends deprecating the flat format.

nodes.label: Observation Merge Order (Two Systems)
nodes.rationale: Two architecturally disconnected observation systems: Python ObservationRegistry+ObservationProvider and Unity ObservationCollector+ObservationProviderBase. Merged in AgentRuntime._build_observation() by strict priority (last write wins). Engine-injected fields (agent_id, inventory etc.) always overwrite everything at priority 4. A provider writing 'agent_id' is silently clobbered — intentional, documented but not enforced.

nodes.label: ActionResult Three Output Channels
nodes.rationale: Every handler returns one ActionResult with three independent channels: state_mutations (AgentRuntime/StateExtension), side_effects (SocialEffectSubscriber via EventBus), engine_commands (HostedWorld→ConnectionHandler→Unity). These channels are independent; a handler can populate any combination. Phase 4 audit flags state_mutations as stringly-typed with implicit conventions — proposes StateMutations typed dataclass.

nodes.label: Brain Protocol (async decide())
nodes.rationale: The Brain protocol requires a single async decide() method. Known design debt: no Brain.cleanup() hook — when an agent is unregistered, its Brain is garbage-collected with no callback to release external resources (persistent HTTP sessions, thread pools). Also: OllamaLLMBrain has no per-call timeout; if Ollama hangs indefinitely, all agents block forever on that tick.

nodes.label: Engine-Owned Ownership Pattern
nodes.rationale: Backend declares every agent in YAML before Unity connects. Unity binds visual shell via BindToExisting. Use when simulation is source of truth, agent count is fixed at deploy time, and backend should tick before Unity connects. Multiple Unity clients can bind the same agents.

nodes.label: Host-Owned Ownership Pattern
nodes.rationale: Backend starts with no agents. Unity owns full agent lifecycle via CreateAtRuntime. Use when Unity determines NPC roster, agent count changes at runtime (procedural spawning), or zero-downtime brain hot-swap is needed (destroy agent, spawn new one with different brain_class, same visual prefab).

nodes.label: Plugin Architecture (Python Protocol Classes)
nodes.rationale: Biomata uses Python Protocol classes as interfaces. Any class path in YAML is dynamically imported — there is no sandboxing. Five extension points: Brain, World, ActionHandler, Memory, ObservationProvider. Plugins registered via YAML class: dotted.module.ClassName; config loader imports and instantiates dynamically.

nodes.label: ActionManifestValidator (Unity Editor Menu Item)
nodes.rationale: Discovers action names by reflecting on the static HandledActions field — a convention used by all built-in handlers. Reflection approach chosen over attribute-based ([BiomataHandles('patrol')]) because the convention already works for all four built-in handlers without code changes; attribute approach deemed unnecessary abstraction for a one-time editor check. Warns (not errors) on unhandled actions because a shared manifest may declare actions not all projects implement.

nodes.label: Phase 4 Naming Debt (Incomplete Renames and Misleading Names)
nodes.rationale: Key issues: (1) ObservationSchema.tags not renamed alongside ActionSchema.required_capabilities — half-complete rename causes contributor confusion. (2) ActionKind implies behavioral constraints that don't exist — advisory LLM label only. (3) state_mutations is stringly-typed with implicit inventory/ext conventions. (4) role.observations is documentation stored as structure — not validated or enforced. (5) AgentOwnershipMode misleads — describes lifecycle control not data ownership.
nodes.norm_label: phase 4 naming debt (incomplete renames and misleading names)
